P267.theorem: A finite positive atomic Stieltjes transform has a unique visible pole-residue measure. Analytic equality on an open interval implies equality of rational continuations and of all principal parts.
P267.boundary: The theorem identifies only visible atoms. Zero-residue and decoupled hidden modes remain unidentifiable.

P269.status: [Proven] minimal outcome count in the five-current subspace; [Strong evidence] shot audit
P269.theorem: M outcome probabilities carry at most M-1 independent real statistics. Five independent currents therefore require at least six outcomes in one POVM; the regular-simplex construction attains the bound.
P269.boundary: Loss, dark-count, and phase calibration remain apparatus obligations. The POVM is a mathematical design, not a built detector.

P270.status: [Proven] rank-defect no-go for linear isometric liftings
P270.theorem: For an isometric embedding E:C^n->C^12, rank(E B E*) is at most n-1 for a Laplacian B. Since the connected strict generator has rank 11, no n<12 lifted reduced Laplacian can equal it, under any scalar normalization.
P270.missing_object: A genuine size-restoring RG comparison must add complement dynamics or an equivalence after quotienting observables; zero-padding or replication alone cannot close the fixed point.

P271.status: [Proven] conditional quantum-information theorem with finite audit
P271.theorem: For a quantum instrument, D(rho||sigma) is at least the classical record divergence plus the record-weighted conditional quantum relative entropies. The remainder is nonnegative by monotonicity under the CPTP instrument channel.
P271.boundary: This is a supplied quantum instrument and not a FIN-derived Hamiltonian, bath, measurement postulate, or laboratory process tensor.

P275.status: [Proven] deterministic exclusion bound for the frozen finite null set
P275.bound: If ||E||_2<=epsilon<lambda_max and 2*sqrt(11)*epsilon/(lambda_max-epsilon)<distance-tolerance, the perturbed null fingerprint cannot enter the acceptance ball.
P275.boundary: This is a certified robustness radius for 400 frozen nulls, not a distribution-free random-matrix false-positive probability.

P276.status: [Proven] two-time semigroup consistency theorem and finite witnesses
P276.theorem: For symmetric positive-definite P1,P2 at calibrated times t1,t2, one homogeneous PSD generator exists iff the matrices commute and log(P2)/t2=log(P1)/t1; when it exists, A=-log(P1)/t1 is unique.
P276.boundary: Two matrices can reject a homogeneous semigroup but do not uniquely identify which adaptive, environmental, or apparatus-memory mechanism caused the defect.
